
### encapsulating w/ app changes  {.smaller}


* application might have special code to handle connecting differently
* + might take advantage of extra information in encapsulation 
<hr class="vspace" />
* example: many application's TLS support
* example: web browser HTTP/SOCKS proxy support


### encapsulating w/o app changes  {.smaller}


* generally: easier to do for lower layers 
<hr class="vspace" />
* link-layer in something 

   * ‘‘virtual’’ (probably Ethernet) device
   * sends/receives from ‘tunnel’

* IP in something 

   * ‘‘virtual’’ IP link
   * destination routing table can go to

* UDP/TCP in something 

   * replace socket API]
   * convince application to connect to different IP address?
   * terminate UDP/TCP connection at ‘wrong’ machine

### Linux tap devices 


```
# create virtual ethernet device mydev
$ ip tuntap add dev mydev mode tap
# mark ethernet device as up
$ ip link set mydev up
$ dhclient mydev # or other commands to use/config device
```

 (dhclient is a DHCP client)
 <hr/>
```
int opentap(const char * name) {
    ... /* setup code, not shown*/
}
...
int fd = opentap("mydev");
...
write(fd, ethernetPacket, packetSize)
/* and (probably in separate threads) */
read(fd, buffer, SIZE); processEthernetPacket(buffer);

```

### Linux tun devices



* same as ‘tap’ devices, but IP, not Ethernet
 
```
# create virtual IP device mydev
$ ip tuntap add dev mydev mode tun
# setup device to be routed to, example:
$ ip address add 10.0.0.2 dev mydev
$ ip route add 10.0.0.0/24 dev mydev
$ ip -6 address add 3fff:1234::1 dev mydev
$ ip -6 route add 3fff:1234::/32 dev mydev

```
<hr/>

* in tunneling program:
  * opens `mydev`
  * read/write IP packets

### full tunnel routing table  {.smaller}

say 198.51.100.5 is running tunnel sever, <br> and 10.0.2.5  is gateway beyond tunnel, <br> and 203.0.113.54 is local gateway: <br>
<table>
<thead>
<tr><th>address</th><th>next hop</th><th>dev</th><th>priority</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><!-- \hline --> 10.0.2.0/24</td><td>---</td><td>tunnel</td><td>normal</td></tr>
<tr><td>198.51.100.5/32</td><td>208.0.113.54</td><td>real</td><td>high</td></tr>
<tr><td>(default)</td><td>203.0.113.54</td><td>real</td><td>normal</td></tr>
<tr><td>(default)</td><td>10.0.2.5</td><td>tunnel</td><td>high</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>


### split tunnel routing table  {.smaller}

say 198.51.100.5 is running tunnel sever, <br> and 10.0.2.5  is gateway beyond tunnel, <br> and 10.0.0.0/16, 198.51.100.0/24 are tunneled networks <br> and 203.0.113.54 is local gateway: <br>

<tr><th>address</th><th>next hop</th><th>dev</th><th>priority</th></tr>

<tr><td>198.51.100.0/24</td><td>10.0.2.5</td><td>tunnel</td><td>normal</td></tr>
<tr><td>198.51.100.5/32</td><td>208.0.113.54</td><td>real</td><td>high</td></tr>
<tr><td>(default)</td><td>203.0.113.54</td><td>real</td><td>normal</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>


### choosing tunnel baesd on source addresses

* shown: telling OS best way to destination is through tunnnel
   * idea: OS automtaically chooses source interface/IP
* alternate idea: application tells OS to use correct interface/IP address
   * servers usually support this to handle multiple IPs

### socket-in-socket  {.smaller}


* example: SSH connection forwarding 
   * <code>ssh -L X:remotehost:remoteport hostname</code>
* example: <code>stunnel</code> for ‘tunneling’ TCP in TLS
* run on port X, configure to connect to some remote host
* configure program to connect to localhost port X
* … instead of remote host

### ‘transparent’ proxy via IP interception  {.smaller}


* example use case: shared HTTP cache used automatically 

   * if company/ISP wants everyone to use cache for performance
   * if company wants to audit all HTTP traffic

* configure router/firewall to direct all HTTP TCP connections to proxy
* either: 

   * configure proxy machine to accept connections on all IP addresses <i>or</i>
   * have router/firewall do network address translation (other direction)

* HTTP proxy <code>squid</code> on Linux, some firewall boxes support this
* I don't think this is a good idea…  

   * problematic with encryption, new HTTP features
